text:
josh_cust: Hey team — during our Dedicated POC for Finvera we are seeing TTFTs that vary a lot. Small prompts ~400ms, but session prompts jump to 6–8s intermittently. Also seeing occasional 429s. We need help diagnosing before the exec demo next Tue. @sara_sales

sara_sales: thanks @josh_cust — adding SE + infra. Can you paste an example request (model, prompt size, conversation length)? Also need approximate qps when this happens.

mike_se: ping — likely two axes: batching window and prefix/KV cache warmup. Which model variant are you running and are you on quantized weights?

josh_cust: model: redwood-medium-v2, quantized int8. Avg prompt tokens 60, convo history sometimes 1200 tokens (they keep long context). Spikes happen at ~60–80 qps peak.

ana_infra: noted. Two quick checks: 1) are you using session affinity? 2) any large initial context prefixes causing cache misses? If requests jump between nodes cache warmup can add TTFT.

lee_oncall: I pulled logs for that customer pool (node-group b):
```
[2024-07-07T14:12:03Z] request_id=abc123 user=finvera code=200 latency_ms=420 cache_hit=true
[2024-07-07T14:12:17Z] request_id=abc456 user=finvera code=429 reason=rate_limit throttle=global window=60s
[2024-07-07T14:12:18Z] request_id=abc457 user=finvera code=200 latency_ms=6100 cache_hit=false prefix_len=118
[2024-07-07T14:12:20Z] request_id=abc458 user=finvera code=200 latency_ms=450 cache_hit=true
```
Looks like short burst triggered limiter then many requests fell back to cold KV path.

mike_se: yep — 429s indicate we crossed the pool-level QPS guardrail. When that happens we do immediate throttling (429) then some requests route to fallback nodes which may not have warmed caches -> high TTFT. Two mitigation ideas: tighten batching (smaller batch window) + enable per-session sticky routing so KV cache follows the session.

ana_infra: Also check their client is not sending a huge history every time. We have a prefix-trimming option: `max_prefix_tokens: 512` to truncate older context before sending to the runtime. That reduces cache churn.

tanvi_product: we can temporarily enable prefix caching on their Dedicated pool and increase burst credits for the demo window. For long-term, recommend reserved capacity with higher baseline throughput or adjusting autoscale thresholds.

sara_sales: quick pricing note for Finvera — reserved capacity will give predictable baseline throughput and come with sustained discount. Burst credits are finite per-reservation period; they help absorbing short spikes but not sustained 80qps over minutes unless sized. I can send a short cost/throughput summary. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

josh_cust: is there a config snippet to try prefix trimming and sticky sessions? we can patch client quickly.

mike_se: paste below — add to runtime route config (example):
```
route_config:
  session_affinity: true
  batching:
    max_batch_window_ms: 10  # reduce latency
    max_batch_tokens: 4096
  prefix_trimming:
    enabled: true
    max_prefix_tokens: 512
```
That should drop most cache misses and reduce TTFT.

ana_infra: I pushed a canary with session_affinity + prefix caching to node-group b at 14:25. deploy-bot: canary finished ok.

deploy-bot: canary deploy completed for node-group b (commit sha: d4f7a9) 

lee_oncall: after canary:
```
[2024-07-07T14:28:10Z] request_id=abc459 code=200 latency_ms=430 cache_hit=true
[2024-07-07T14:28:22Z] request_id=abc460 code=200 latency_ms=480 cache_hit=true
[2024-07-07T14:28:45Z] request_id=abc461 code=200 latency_ms=520 cache_hit=true
```
Looks much better; 429s disappeared from sampled window.

tanvi_product: for the security QA — Finvera asked for SOC2 attestation and key management details. @ana_infra can you attach the SOC2 link and KMS/HSM bullet points in the thread?

ana_infra: will do. Short answer: SOC2 Type II report available under NDA, TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, KMS integration (customer-managed keys supported for Private deployments), option for HSM via partner. I’ll DM the specific docs and upload to the deal folder.

sara_sales: great — next steps: 1) Mike — follow up with a short runbook for client-side trimming + config snippet, 2) Ana — share SOC2 + KMS docs, 3) I’ll update pricing proposal with reserved capacity vs burst cost, 4) Josh — can we do a 30m sync tomorrow to validate?

josh_cust: yes tomorrow 10am PT works. Appreciate the quick turn. :pray:

mike_se: I’ll also add a monitoring alert for cache_miss_rate > 10% to warn before demo.

lee_oncall: keeping an eye on errors, will escalate if 429s surface again. :thumbsup:

sara_sales: thanks everyone — marking as in-progress on deal thread and looping security for the questionnaire.

josh_cust: thanks team — will send the client-side change and confirm tomorrow."
